references.text: Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is mentioned together with Joshua as the only spies who believed that God could give them the land.
God promises that Caleb will be allowed to enter the land because of his faithfulness and a different spirit.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is one of the two who will be allowed to enter the promised land.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, survived along with Joshua among the spies.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is mentioned as one of only a few survivors from the first census.
Caleb is described as a Kenite who followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is appointed to distribute the land for the tribe of Judah.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, is promised the land he has walked on because he followed the Lord wholeheartedly.
Caleb recalls the promise made to him through Moses and receives Hebron as his inheritance.
Caleb, son of Jephunneh, receives his portion of the tribe of Judah's inheritance and drives out the three sons of Anak.
Caleb gives his daughter Achsah to Othniel, who captured Kiriath-sepher.
